title: Google Launches Gemini 4 Hydrogen, Its Fast Model for Agentic Work
excerpt: Hydrogen takes the execution tier of the Gemini 4 family: faster than the old Flash line, priced at $1.50/$7.50 per million tokens, and now running inside Google Search for all users.
body:
• Google has launched Gemini 4 Hydrogen, the fast execution tier of its Gemini 4 family, built for everyday coding and agentic workflows rather than frontier reasoning.
  • Google says Hydrogen scores 51 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at its default high setting — ahead of the frontier Argon model's 50 — and finishes tasks 2.5 times faster than Gemini 3.8 Flash.
  • It is priced at $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens across a 1 million-token context window, with four thinking levels up to a new xhigh tier.
  • Hydrogen is rolling out now in the Gemini API and AI Studio, the Gemini app, Google Antigravity for paid subscribers, and Google Search for all users.

Google introduced Gemini 4 Hydrogen on November 12, positioning it as the daily driver of the Gemini 4 family. Where its frontier models, Gemini 4 Carbon and Gemini 4 Argon, are built for deep, long-horizon reasoning, Hydrogen is built for rapid execution: writing code, running tests, verifying changes and carrying multi-step agent tasks to completion, according to Google's launch announcement.

The headline numbers

Google reports that Hydrogen surpasses Argon on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at its default high thinking level, 51 to 50, and reaches 54 at its new xhigh setting, the highest of its four thinking levels (low, medium, high and xhigh). Against the model it replaces, Gemini 3.8 Flash, Google says Hydrogen finishes tasks 2.5 times faster at the high setting and more than triples its Terminal-Bench 4.1 score, 57% against 18.2%, while cutting fabricated claims by more than five times. These are Google's own benchmark figures; independent evaluations will follow as third parties test the model. The model pairs a native 1 million-token input window with up to 1 million output tokens, aimed at synthesising dense PDFs, spreadsheets, charts, audio and video into structured deliverables, and ranks fifth on arena.ai's Agent Arena live benchmark, Google said.

"On Terminal-Bench 4.0, Google said Orchestrator reached near-Carbon task success rates while using 24% less quota and finishing 19% faster."

Orchestrator: models working in teams

Alongside Hydrogen, Google introduced Orchestrator in Google Antigravity, which switches dynamically between models inside a single development session — Carbon coordinating, Hydrogen powering worker and verifier agents that build and test changes in parallel across isolated workspaces. On Terminal-Bench 4.0, Google said Orchestrator reached near-Carbon task success rates while using 24% less quota and finishing 19% faster. Coverage of the launch by FoneArena notes the same split: frontier models for architectural judgement, Hydrogen for the high-volume execution work around it.

What changes for everyday users

Hydrogen is also the new engine inside Google Search, which Google calls its biggest model upgrade to Search yet: better handling of multi-part questions, typos and highly specific instructions, more visual responses, and a wider fan-out of links. In the Gemini app, Google says the model follows tone and format instructions more closely, pulls context from Gmail, Google Drive and connected apps such as Airtable and Dropbox, and produces working interface prototypes in fewer prompts. On safety, Google says Hydrogen reduces overreach in agentic tasks by up to 81% compared with 3.8 Flash and is more than 2.3 times as resilient to indirect prompt injection on the Gray Swan benchmark.

Price and availability

Hydrogen is priced flat across its full context window at $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens. It is available to developers through the Gemini API in AI Studio across all tiers and in Android Studio, to paid Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers in Antigravity and Gemini in Google Sheets, to enterprises through Gemini for business, and to everyone in the Gemini app and Google Search, Google said.
